When on, a small bubble appears on screen. Tap it to save the clipboard, write a note, record audio or open the inbox. Tap anywhere else and it tucks into a slim tab at the edge; tap the tab to expand it. The bubble hides while you\'re in ZhiCun.\nEnabling the bubble also brings it back automatically after a restart or app update. Turning this switch off turns off auto-restore as well (to keep the bubble without auto-restore, turn off \"Restore bubble after restart\" below).
Brings the bubble back after a restart or app update. Turning it off doesn\'t remove the bubble, but it won\'t reappear until you open ZhiCun.

When on, tapping the bubble saves the clipboard text as a record (the same content isn\'t saved twice, and the system may ask you to confirm pasting). If the clipboard is empty, tapping expands the panel. When off, tapping only expands the panel and never reads the clipboard.
When on, the bubble won\'t tuck into the edge when you tap elsewhere — it stays a full circle. Turn it off to restore the original behavior: any tap elsewhere shrinks it into a slim tab.

When on, pressing the full bubble for more than half a second starts recording; releasing stops and saves it as a voice note (a timer appears at the top while recording). Very short recordings aren\'t saved. Long-press doesn\'t work on the slim tab.
Overlay permission: not granted — enable it in system settings
Allow \"Display over other apps\" in system settings first

The bubble relies on a foreground service and comes back after a restart or app update. Many systems treat swiping the app away from Recents as a force stop; pull the card down and tap the lock to keep it. After a force stop, open ZhiCun once to bring it back.

The bubble relies on a foreground service. \"Restore bubble after restart\" is off, so after a restart or app update you need to open ZhiCun once for the bubble to reappear. Many systems treat swiping the app away from Recents as a force stop; pull the card down and tap the lock to keep it.

The most effective step: add the ZhiCun widget to your home screen first (long-press an empty spot → Widgets → drag the ZhiCun widget out), then in the system\'s app launch manager turn on auto-start, associated start and background activity for ZhiCun. With the widget in place the system treats ZhiCun as a resident app, and swiping it away from Recents usually leaves the bubble running.

Allow sending content to the cloud
When on, text in your records is sent to the cloud for summaries, tags and semantic indexing, and voice recordings are uploaded for transcription. Search terms are also sent to compute similarity.
When off: summaries, AI tags, semantic search and voice transcription stop immediately.

Off. Neither new nor existing records are uploaded; keyword search and on-device text recognition still work. Fetching web page text still requests the page from its site — that step is independent of this switch. Records that may contain sensitive information aren\'t requested until you tap \"Allow fetching this page\" on their detail page.
Records that may contain sensitive information aren\'t uploaded by default; confirm them one by one on the detail page. That requires the switch above to be on and the AI gateway to be reachable.
Transcription runs in the cloud and follows the \"Allow sending content to the cloud\" switch above; there\'s no separate switch.
Original records, images and audio exist only on this device. Content is sent to the cloud only while the switch above is on.

1. Record text, images and audio are stored in the app's private directory. They do not enter the system gallery and are excluded from system backups.
2. While the switch is on, only two kinds of content are sent to the AI gateway: record text (for summaries, tags and the semantic index) and audio (for transcription).
3. When you save a web link, the app requests the page from that site (main text and images): the request carries only the URL, never the record text. This step is independent of the switch above and also happens when cloud AI is off.
4. Records that may contain sensitive information (ID numbers, bank card numbers, API keys, etc.) are neither uploaded nor fetched from their URL by default. Both need a separate confirmation on the detail page: allowing the fetch releases only this one request to that site, and the fetched text stays on the phone; allowing upload releases only what is sent to the AI gateway, and requires the switch above to be on and the gateway to be available.
5. Semantic search sends your query to the cloud to compute similarity with existing records.
6. To count usage separately per device (so that all devices do not share one rate limit), the app generates a random device identifier and sends it with requests; the gateway stores only its salted hash (which cannot be traced back to a specific device) to count requests and installs. It keeps it for 365 days and records no content or account information.
7. Turning the switch off stops all of the above immediately; existing records, summaries and search results are unaffected.
8. Uninstalling the app deletes its private directory; export first if you want to keep your data.
9. Feedback goes through your email app; whether to send it is entirely up to you.

On: use the official gateway (enter its URL and access token) — ready to use. Off: fill in your own service for each of the three capabilities; summaries, embeddings and transcription can come from different vendors.
Leave blank to keep the saved token

The three configurations are independent; fill in only the ones you need. Groups left blank will not send requests. API keys are stored on this device and encrypted, and saved keys are never shown again.
Text is sent here to generate summaries, short titles and tags (OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint).
Records and search queries are sent here to compute embeddings (/embeddings endpoint). After changing models, old vectors cannot be compared and must be rebuilt below.
Audio is sent here to be transcribed (/audio/transcriptions endpoint, multipart upload).
Leave blank to keep the saved key
Chat endpoints come in two common formats; pick the one your vendor actually provides. Some models support both. Embeddings and transcription are OpenAI-compatible only.
